topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
transcript:
Header: 2026-04-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kumar (Redwood SE), Jordan Lewis (Polaris Head of ML), Maya Patel (Platform Eng), Samir Rao (Security)

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we really appreciate you making time. I'm Alex from Redwood - I'm the AE on the account.
00:07 Jordan Lewis: Hey Alex thanks, excited to learn more. We saw the quickstart on your site, curious about free credits and how fast we can get to first token.
00:14 Priya Kumar: Hi Jordan, Maya, Samir — I'm Priya on the solutions engineering side. Today we'll walk through the self-serve flow, what a PLG quickstart looks like, and the differences when you want Dedicated or Private later.
00:23 Maya Patel: Quick note, our team runs services in GCP us-central, we have strict egress controls and a KMS for keys.
00:30 Samir Rao: And security - SOC2 required, SSO/SAML for console access, audit logs are must-haves.
00:37 Alex Chen: Totally — those are common. Quick overview: hosted Redwood API gives you immediate access (self-serve), you can sign up, get free credits, create an API key and call the text/chat/embeddings endpoints. Time-to-first-token is usually minutes — you can run a curl or our SDK and stream responses.
00:55 Jordan Lewis: When you say minutes, is that with an internal approval step or totally self-serve?
00:59 Priya Kumar: Fully self-serve for the hosted API. You sign up, verify email, the free credits appear on the account. For Dedicated you need an order/contract which takes longer. Private (VPC/on-prem) is the longest path due to network and compliance setup.
01:15 Maya Patel: For our POC we want to be live in dev in under two days ideally. Could be fine to use hosted if data residency and PII masking are OK.
01:25 Priya Kumar: That sounds reasonable. For dev/testing many customers use hosted with data retention controls and optional redact rules. If you have PHI or strict residency we recommend Private.
01:35 Jordan Lewis: Latency expectations: our assistant needs sub-300ms median for 256-token responses. Can Redwood hit that on hosted?
01:42 Priya Kumar: Depends on model and sequence length. For smaller open models and optimized runtimes we often see 80-200ms token rates at modest load; for larger models 300-500ms. We can run a quick benchmark in the pilot.
02:00 Alex Chen: Important trade-off: latency vs cost vs model quality. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost for heavy traffic; hosted is easiest for quickstart.
02:12 Maya Patel: If we start hosted, how do we later move to Dedicated without rework?
02:16 Priya Kumar: It's designed to be seamless — same API surface, you pin model versions and route policies in the console. Migration is mostly config, not code changes.
02:26 Samir Rao: On encryption: do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private or Dedicated?
02:31 Priya Kumar: Yes, Private supports customer KMS, Dedicated can integrate with KMS for key wrapping depending on contract. Hosted uses platform-managed keys by default; we have an enterprise option.
02:44 Jordan Lewis: What about SSO and RBAC?
02:47 Alex Chen: SSO (SAML/Okta) and granular RBAC are available for Dedicated/Private, hosted has SSO for enterprise accounts and role controls in the Console. We'll share the doc.
02:58 Jordan Lewis: Any gotchas on the quickstart? We want to hand the devs a reproducible script.
03:03 Priya Kumar: The quickstart script does: create account, claim free credits, generate API key, run SDK sample (python or node) and a curl streaming example. We also include a small eval harness to run 100 sample prompts so you can measure latency and cost baseline. Typically time-to-first-token is ~2-10 minutes depending on email verification steps.
03:20 Jordan Lewis: Nice. For the pilot, we'd like to test two dimensions: latency at 256 tokens and cost per 1k requests. Also want to test caching and batching since our queries have similar prefixes.
03:31 Priya Kumar: We can enable prefix/KV caching in the runtime and show quantization profiles to reduce unit cost. We'll propose a pilot config: 1 week, 50k tokens/day baseline, 512 token cap, target median latency <300ms for chosen model.
03:46 Maya Patel: Does Redwood expose token-level cost in the dashboard? We need that granularity for internal chargebacks.
03:50 Alex Chen: Yes, Console has token-level cost and latency breakdown per route/model. You can export CSVs or hook into our billing API.
03:58 Jordan Lewis: Security: can you provide SOC2 and ISO docs? Also need audit logs retention options.
04:03 Alex Chen: We'll send SOC2 report and security whitepaper. Audit logs retention is configurable — enterprise tiers have longer retention.
04:12 Samir Rao: For Hosted flow, are requests ever routed through vendor-managed clusters outside region? We need EU residency for some data.
04:19 Priya Kumar: You can choose region for hosted endpoints and we offer EU regions. For strict residency we recommend Private. We'll note this in the pilot plan.
04:28 Jordan Lewis: Pricing — ballpark per 1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated commit?
04:33 Alex Chen: Ballpark: hosted public rates vary by model class; we'll share the pricing sheet. Dedicated is typically lower per-token with a monthly commit. I'll include a few example compute/price breakouts in the follow-up.
04:45 Maya Patel: Any performance tuning we should do client-side? For example, batch requests vs streaming?
04:50 Priya Kumar: Continuous batching and proper connection reuse help. For chat workloads we'd recommend streaming responses (keep latency low) and use batching for high-throughput offline generation.
05:01 Jordan Lewis: Who owns the pilot internally? We expect Jordan + Maya to coordinate devs, Samir will review security.
05:07 Jordan Lewis: Yes we'll own it. Aim to run pilot next week if we can get creds and a plan.
05:12 Alex Chen: Great — recap next steps: we'll send quickstart link & free credits, security docs (SOC2/KMS), pilot proposal with benchmark config and pricing. Priya will schedule pilot planning.
05:22 Priya Kumar: I'll also include a short checklist for the developers: sample code, SDK install, common gotchas (CORS, long responses, token limits).
05:30 Jordan Lewis: One more — any reference customers in regulated spaces? Helps our security team trust the path.
05:36 Alex Chen: Yes, we have customers in fintech and health; I'll share anonymized case studies and references once we have NDA in place.
05:45 Maya Patel: Good.
05:46 Samir Rao: Thanks all.
05:48 Alex Chen: Thanks everyone we'll follow up with the materials and calendar invites.

Notes: slight transcription noise — some product names transcribed like 'Readwood' or 'Red wood Dedi'. There are brief crosstalk overlaps.

Recap (end):
- Host quickstart is self-serve; free credits will be made available to Polaris Tech to validate POC.
- Pilot scope: 1 week, 50k tokens/day baseline, test latency and cost; measure caching/quantization impact.
- Security: send SOC2, KMS options, SSO and audit logs details.
- Next steps and owners listed in action items.

References mentioned during call: quickstart guide (link to be sent), pricing spreadsheet (to be sent), SOC2 and security whitepaper (to be sent), pilot benchmark template (to be shared).
